title: Security headers
description: Framework-neutral TypeScript builder for HTTP response security headers: validated Content-Security-Policy with per-request nonces and report-only mode, HSTS, nosniff, Referrer-Policy, Permissions-Policy, COOP, and X-Frame-Options, applied to Fetch Responses.

notes: Uses standard Fetch Response/Headers, crypto.getRandomValues, and btoa; intended for Node.js 22+, Bun, Deno, Cloudflare Workers, Next.js middleware/route handlers, and Hono. Only Node.js 22 was exercised by repository tests.
securityHeaders() returns a plain record usable with any server that sets headers, including Node http and Express res.set().
No runtime packages, environment reads, or network access.

configuration: csp merges per directive over default-src 'self'; object-src 'none'; base-uri 'self'; frame-ancestors 'none'; form-action 'self'. A directive set to false is removed, true emits a valueless directive, and csp: false omits the header.
nonce (from createNonce, generated per response) is appended to nonceDirectives (default script-src); the application must put the same nonce on its script tags.
reportOnly sends Content-Security-Policy-Report-Only. hsts defaults to max-age=31536000; includeSubDomains, preload is opt-in, and hsts: false omits it for plain-HTTP development.

referrerPolicy, permissionsPolicy (merged over camera/microphone/geolocation/payment/usb/browsing-topics disabled), crossOriginOpenerPolicy, frameOptions, and contentTypeOptions can each be changed or disabled with false.
withSecurityHeaders preserves existing response headers unless override: true. Invalid configuration throws a TypeError.
limitations: Default CSP blocks inline scripts/styles and third-party resources; applications must add their actual sources or nonces and test every page, ideally in reportOnly first.
Validation rejects separators, whitespace, and control characters in tokens, but does not judge whether a source such as 'unsafe-inline', 'unsafe-eval', or * is safe.
includeSubDomains in the default HSTS affects every subdomain once a browser sees it; disable or shorten it before all subdomains serve HTTPS. Preload submission is not performed.
No CSP violation report collector, Report-To/Reporting-Endpoints management, CORS, COEP/CORP, or cookie attribute handling is included.
withSecurityHeaders transfers the original body stream and returns Responses with a status outside 200-599 unchanged. Tests ran on Node.js 22 only; browser enforcement was not exercised.
decisions: default CSP default-src 'self' blocks inline scripts/styles and third-party resources
HSTS max-age=31536000; includeSubDomains by default; X-Frame-Options DENY; COOP same-origin
Referrer-Policy strict-origin-when-cross-origin; existing headers win unless override: true
no CORS, COEP/CORP or cookie attributes
